paragraphs: The 318i has been a mainstay of the 3 Series diesel range since 2012, spanning two generations under one badge. Early F30/F31 models from 2012 to 2015 use the N47, a 2.0-litre diesel that's part of a family known for a specific timing chain issue. From late 2015 onwards, across both the F30/F31 and later the G20/G21, the 318i switched to the B47, a newer, significantly more reliable unit that doesn't share the N47's timing chain concerns. Knowing which one your car has matters, because the components and the known wear pattern differ - which is exactly why we confirm your exact engine by registration before quoting.
about.boldParagraph: The 318i is no longer in production, but we continue to rebuild and replace engines for every one still on the road.

cards.body: A 2.0-litre turbocharged four-cylinder petrol engine fitted to the 318i from 2012 to 2015. The N20 has a well-documented pattern of timing chain guide failure, which we address as standard on every N20 rebuild by replacing the timing chain, guides, and tensioners.

A 2.0-litre turbocharged four-cylinder petrol engine that replaced the N20 from 2015 onward. Fitted to both the late F30/F31 generation and the current G20/G21. The B48 is a significantly more robust engine and is generally considered reliable.

compatibility.intro: Because the 318i spans two distinct engines across its production run, fitting the wrong replacement — or assuming an N20 part will work on a B48 car — risks a compatibility problem that's expensive to unpick. Before we quote or supply anything, we confirm:

points.text: Your exact engine code (N20 or B48) via registration or VIN
Any electronics or ECU considerations specific to your exact build

compatibility.footer: This is why we always start with your registration rather than a generic 318i quote — it protects you from paying for parts that don't fit your actual car.
